Parktown Boys: The passing of Enock Mpianzi

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A boys loses his life at parktown boys high school

Unique Selling Point:
The truth about what happened to ENOCK Mpianzi is a factual matrix of alleged eye-witness accounts, allegations and statements from those who were ultimately responsible to ensure the boys safety.

We unpack exactly what happened that day on the river and talk to Enocks family about the final hours before they found his body in the crocodile river.

Justice will take its course, but nothing will bring back their son

Extra Budget Items:
1/2 day with Claire

Yves Mpianzi Mpianzi

Script:



Time code Character/
Visual
1 00:00:00 Enoch pictures V/O: When 13 year old grade 8 pupil in Enock Mpianzi
was dropped off at Parktown boys high school to go to his orientation camp they could have imagined that they would never see him again. This is the last video Yves Kadilo of his older brother and best friend took of him before he died
2 00:00:30 Yves If atleast People who knows the truth the real truth about his death. Can step up And just like confess. Just tell us the truth. That's that's all we need
3 00:00:48 VO At this point the truth about what happened after Enock boarded the bus to when his body was found three days later. Lies somewhere within a factual matrix of disparities between eyewitness accounts from the boys at the camp and statements made by those in charge of the boys at the time. The owner's at Nyati Bush get away river lodge and Parktown boys high school.
4 00:01:08 V/O Barry which is not his real name to protect had family who were on the camp according to him all the boys that were on the camp have been instructed not to talk about what happened beyond these gates.
5 00:01:18 Barry Since Monday school is in a complete blackout. They don't let any information to go out to social media and to media to media as well. All the kids in school were told not to speak to anyone even to their own parents.
6 00:01:32 We were instructed by the department of education that non of the families from. Park Town boys high school are allowed to speak to us.
7 00:01:41 Claire On Wednesday the 15th of January. Enock Mpianzi arrived here at the Nyati Bush Lodge with over 100 other grade 8 for what was supposed to be the start of his journey at Parktown boys high.
8 00:01:54 Barry The kids will explain what to do. As the activities of the day and they've been told they're going to be doing some some kind of water activity and they would explain to them about that they have to build their own rafts and they do racing in the water and they would divide into groups of twelve.
9 00:02:12 V/O The children were given bamboo sticks and rope and then also told to use their own shoelaces to build these makeshift rafts.
10 00:02:20 Barry So one person will be on the top of the raft and the other eleven boys have to swim to push their raft into the water to the point where the race should end.
11 00:02:30 V/O We repeatedly asked the owner of Nyati Bush break and River Lodge and Anton Knoezte for an interview but he declined. He did however shared this version of events with us off camera.
12 00:02:41 Claire link According to Anton Knoetze This was supposed to be a running activity and not a water activity and that is why the boys were not wearing any safety gear. The boys were told to come down this path running with their makeshift raft and they were supposed to enter the river. At this point what Anton was been told by his camp facilitators is that the boys were instructed to run along the river bank in the shallow water and come out in the opposite side where we see the two poles
13 00:03:10 V/O According to Professor Graham Addison a river adventure specialist, Antons explanation for not assuring the children with lifejackets is not valid. He also raised other red flags with regards to what international standards were not followed that day on the river
14 00:03:25 Graham At an absolute minimum. They should have had a lifejacket and even non swimmers can use those and they're fine. Also they need to be asked some questions can they swim? Can they get out there in the water? And do they panic? because that would be a bad sign and then they would need to be carefully looked after. Do they know each other. We would always insist on a buddy system where one looks after the other and would report another one to be missing.
15 00:03:51 Claire Now the water was much shallower than what we see now but what we were told by Anton is that the boys got quite competitive and instead of just sticking to the shallow end they overtook one another which meant that some of them went into the deeper parts of the river and that's where all the trouble started.
16 00:04:08 Graham Well I ask you how do we know where the shallow water is? Even if we've you know even if we can see the current we don't know whether it's deep there or shallow there. So the rescuers would have to keep them or rather than the guides would have to keep them in the shallow water if that was the intention.
17 00:04:27 V/O None of the facilitators that the camp had placed along the course were actually qualified lifeguards or river guides. There was simply camp facilitators who according to Anton know the river well once the children went into the deep water they got caught in the currents and many landed up in trouble
18 00:04:45 Barry Kids who are all over the water and some of them could not swim. Some other kids dived in to save their own friends and some kids some adults who even a life coach waited for the kids to get out of the water or get out of the water. We tried to pulling the kids out of the water
19 00:05:02 V/O we received this audio recording from a group of mothers that spoke to the boys when they returned from the camp On Friday the 17th of January
20 00:05:10 Recording But then we were also many boys that were saving each other

There 14 boys on the island waiting to be saved.

There was another 2

Twenty that were like floating because they couldn’t swim, on the riverbank so they had to pull them in with sticks

He told me that he saw Enock going but then the thing is that her tried to get Enock but he couldn’t

So he rather just went from another boy and then theyt said that Enock went down the river separate, enock went down the one side the facilitator went down the other side

Rememeber there were these other two teachers playing with rocks while the children were drowning
21 00:05:49 Claire link According to the sources we spoke to no roll call was done when the boys boarded the bus at Park Town boys high school. No roll call was done when they arrived here at the Nyati Bush and river break. The first time roll call was taken was 5 p.m. on Wednesday evening an hour after the river activity
23 00:06:08 Recording When they read Enock’s name and it was quiet then they repeated it and they asked where he is some people said he didn’t come some people said he was missing
24 00:06:19 So even though Enock was not present when enroll was done and an eyewitness report claims that the informed the principal that enough was missing on Wednesday. No search party was started. Sebastian, Enocks godfather and pastor
25 00:06:35 Claire and Sebastian When was the next time that the family got communication was it on the Thursday.

Sebastian: It was on Thursday, 10am he reciebved a call from the facility willing to confirm if Enock did take part of the journey which led to the schooling camp He said yes. My son is with you there because I put him myself in the bus and his bag in the trailer. So the conversation ended. Bye. Okay we will call you later. There is something here about your son. But if we call you later maybe it means something is wrong. But hold on let us invest to get around so 4:00pm. They called him to confirm that Enoch has gone missing.
26 00:07:34 V/O Together with Enocks parents Sebastian is one of the first people at the camp looking for Enock on Thursday evening
27 00:07:40 Sebastian I remember when I was searching for him on the river. I told the policeman I can't go and leave Enock in the wood. I don't believe. Allow me to shout his name. Maybe he can hear me from somewhere. I was thinking that he's hanging somewhere on the grass or what. So the police say Carry on. That will help us. Then I start shouting Enock Enock.
28 00:08:07 Claire More than 40 hours after he was last seen Enock Mpianzi body was found submerged in the river where the raft making activity had taken place.
29 00:08:17 Sebastian It's not easy to digest such a reality. He died unnoticed or unattended.
30 00:08:32 Yves We want justice for my brother all we need is justice.
31 00:08:43 V/O Enocks family are exploring their legal options, at this point They have approached the South African Human Rights Commission, Gushwell Brooks is their spokesperson
32 00:08:52 Gushwell brooks As tragic as the matter is and of course thers many legal. Aspects whether there is negligence in the form of deal probably in the form of criminology or culpable homicide the fact of the matter is we felt that there is a mere violation of human rights in this instance. I think. There was a responsibility on behalf of the school, the facility to ensure that they protect. Those particular rights

Claire: so then who is alternately responsible here? Who had locus parental here

Gushwell: based on the law the school assumes role of locus parents the school is responsible the school take responsibility and custody of this child and they therefore have to exercise every reasonable measure to ensure the safety and well being of. The child
33 00:09:37 Voice over Because he was ultimately responsible for the boy’s safety At a press conference held on Friday the Gauteng education MEC Panyaza Lesufi confirmed what immediate action would
be taken against the principle of Parktown boys high
34 00:09:50 Lesufi We have taken a decision to immediately suspend the principle
35 00:09:55 V/O He also confirmed that the camp was in fact not even authorized
36 00:09:59 Lesufi By the time the school embarked on this trip the district and head office had not approved. The trip.
37 00:10:08 v/o As a result, the district officials involved have been suspended
And all the teachers that were present at the camp will be individually investigated
38 00:10:17 Claire link The Gauteng MEC for education Panyazi Lesufi has said that no body is immune to their ongoing investigation into the death of Enock Mpianzi from the Department of Education, the school governing body to park town boys high school
39 00:10:32 V/O But while justice runs its course, nothing will bring this families son back.
40 00:10:36 Yves Nothing can remove what is lost in the puzzle. Our mother was the only lady in the family, four boys. We were a perfect family and. There's nothing nothing that can ever replace him
41 00:10:48 Sebastian No matter, Negligence or Accident or accident the result is a 13 year old. Ambitious young man. Is gone unoticed

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A boys loses his life at parktown boys high school
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The truth about what happened to ENOCK Mpianzi is a factual matrix of alleged eye-witness accounts, allegations and statements from those who were ultimately responsible to ensure the boys safety. We unpack exactly what happened that day on the river and talk to Enocks family about the final hours before they found his body in the crocodile river. Justice will take its course, but nothing will bring back their son
